title: Princeton University community rallies for doctoral student in ICE custody

tea.why: A Princeton University doctoral student was detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.
tea.want: Protesters demanded the release of the detained doctoral student.
tea.changed: Nov 23, 2026: More than 100 people rallied at Princeton University to call for the release of Eva Yi Xie.

summary: Members of the Princeton University community gathered on campus near the Princeton School of Public and International Affairs to demand the release of third-year Ph.D. student Eva Yi Xie. Xie was taken into custody by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement at Ronald Reagan National Airport after attending a neuroscience conference. Rally participants, including students, faculty members, and colleagues, described her as gentle and brilliant, expressing shock over her detention. The protest was organized by members of the Princeton Progressive Coalition. Following the demonstration, attendees participated in a phone bank to contact federal representatives, and organizers distributed LED candles as a symbol of hope. The Department of Homeland Security stated that Xie was admitted temporarily in 2016 and never held valid study authorization, while her attorney argued she has a pending asylum application permitting her to remain.
demands: Release Eva Yi Xie from ICE custody
response: The Department of Homeland Security stated that Xie was admitted temporarily in 2016, was required to leave that year, and has never held valid study authorization. CBS News Philadelphia reported awaiting a response regarding detention conditions.

crowd.text: More than 100 people showed up to a rally Monday

updates.text: More than 100 people gathered at Princeton University to protest the detention of a doctoral student.
